isolation: the greeter service is stateless (no persisted data); each scenario issues its own independent GET request and asserts only on that request's own response, so no cross-scenario state exists to isolate

scenarios.rule: Calling /hello with a name returns a greeting addressed to that name

steps.text: the greeter service is running
an API Consumer calls GET /hello with name "Ada"
the response is a JSON greeting addressed to "Ada"
steps.command: curl -s -G "$BASE/hello" --data-urlencode "name=Ada" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d=={'name':'Ada','message':'Hello, Ada!'}"

scenarios.rule: Calling /hello without a name still returns a valid greeting

steps.text: the greeter service is running
an API Consumer calls GET /hello with no name parameter
the response is a JSON greeting addressed to "World"
steps.command: curl -s "$BASE/hello" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d=={'name':'World','message':'Hello, World!'}"

scenarios.rule: An explicitly empty name is treated the same as an omitted name
scenarios.scenario: Greeting with an explicitly empty name

steps.text: the greeter service is running
an API Consumer calls GET /hello with name ""
the response is a JSON greeting addressed to "World"
steps.command: curl -s -G "$BASE/hello" --data-urlencode "name=" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d=={'name':'World','message':'Hello, World!'}"

scenarios.rule: A very long name is accepted and echoed in full
scenarios.scenario: Greeting a caller with a very long name

steps.text: the greeter service is running
an API Consumer calls GET /hello with a name that is 2000 characters long, all the letter "a"
the response is a JSON greeting addressed to that same 2000-character name
steps.command: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/story4_resp.txt')); assert d['name']=='a'*2000; assert d['message']=='Hello, '+'a'*2000+'!'"
steps.observed: name field length 2000, all 'a', message == 'Hello, ' + 2000 a's + '!'

scenarios.rule: The service exposes a health check

an API Consumer calls GET /health
the response reports the service status as healthy
steps.command: curl -s "$BASE/health" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['status']=='healthy'"

scenarios.scenario: An unrelated query parameter does not change the greeting

an API Consumer calls GET /hello with name "Ada" and an extra parameter "foo" set to "bar"

steps.command: curl -s -G "$BASE/hello" --data-urlencode "name=Ada" --data-urlencode "foo=bar" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d=={'name':'Ada','message':'Hello, Ada!'}"
